summary: Implemented the Kong et al. (2015) refined geometry as the Issue #166 project interpretation: a five-layer regular hexagonal 30-bead body plus three 30-bead flagella for 120 total beads. The 2015 profiles use center-layer 120-degree attachment slots, configurable 0.25 b hooks, 0.29 b flagellum bonds, and disabled diagonal braces. Actual topology is recorded in single-run and campaign manifests, replay validates regenerated bead counts, and both pending profiles are evaluation_ready for Issue #168 without promotion to supported. User review follow-up sets the project profile to the posterior helix-axis initial condition, enlarges the 3D review view while preserving the whole geometry, records tau_s in 3D timestamps, and uses the Phase 3 body_capsule_orthographic_v1 contract for 2D review images. Codex Cloud feedback was addressed by keeping every non-2015 pending profile blocked in both the manifest and execution validator.
non_blocking_issues: Issue #168 motor-off 0.1 tau, motor-on 1 tau, long-time stability, brace adoption, and supported promotion were not run or decided.
The paper text describes a pentagonal refined body, while Issue #166 intentionally adopts a hexagonal five-layer body from Fig. 1, the 30-body-bead count, and the five-layer interpretation.

The one-step total-force residual (9.8870e-14 N) is dominated by the existing finite-difference torsion force. The paper motor component itself balances to 1.8425e-26 N net force and 7.7421e-33 N m net torque. Torsion stability and acceptance remain part of Issue #168.

user_review_points: The step-1 images were inspected and show the refined six-slot body with three 30-bead flagella; neither image uses the 2010 triangular body.

The render-only follow-up images show the full refined geometry at 7 um view range, an unclipped t/tau_s label, the posterior project initial condition, the unchanged lateral paper initial condition, and the Phase 3-compatible centered body capsule 2D image.
Long-time body deformation, bundling, propulsion, collapse, and fly-away behavior cannot be determined from a one-step render and are deferred to Issue #168.
